Definition: a Sukkite, or inhabitant of some place near Egypt (i.e. hut-dwellers)
BiblicalUsage: A Sukkite is one of the peoples who come up with Shishak against Jerusalem in Rehoboam's fifth year. The name appears once, in the list of the invading host. They are hut-dwellers, and they come against the city that has forsaken God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Sukkites matter because even a people named for huts is part of the judgment God sends on a faithless king.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
